title: Superposition and the Hadamard Gate
summary: The states |+⟩ and |−⟩ and a quantum random number generator.
mission: Build a 3-bit quantum random number generator: put all three qubits in a uniform superposition and measure each one into the classical bit with the same index. The 8 outcomes (000 to 111) must be equally likely.
hints: The Hadamard gate takes |0⟩ to the state |+⟩, on the equator of the sphere: qc.h(0). Each qubit needs its own Hadamard.
To read the result, measure each qubit and store the value in a classical bit: qc.measure(qubit, bit). That is three qubits and three bits.
The solution applies qc.h(0), qc.h(1) and qc.h(2), then qc.measure(0, 0), qc.measure(1, 1) and qc.measure(2, 2). A loop for q in range(3) avoids the repetition.

prediction.question: You prepare |+⟩ and measure 100 times: you get 56 zeros and 44 ones. Is the generator biased?
options: Yes: a fair generator would give exactly 50 zeros
No: it is normal statistical fluctuation, 56 is about 1.2 standard deviations from 50
It would only be biased if more than 60 zeros appeared
prediction.explanation: With N = 100 and p = 1/2, the standard deviation is σ = √(N p (1−p)) = 5. Getting 56 zeros means being 6 above 50, about 1.2σ: quite common. A fair generator almost never gives exactly 50, and the relative gap shrinks as N grows.
